catalysts: Further BoC communication that energy pass-through and global tightening outweigh the August labor contraction.
US data that keep the Fed path from being faded, forcing Canada to close more of the 2.29-versus-3.85 overnight gap.
Canadian activity/inflation prints that confirm Q2 GDP and 3% headline rather than the employment -42k signal.

context_build.causal_mechanism: Test whether Canada has eased too far relative to a still-expanding, still-inflating global cycle. Verified fact: CORRA overnight is 2.29 as of 2026-09-17, August headline CPI held at 3.0% y/y, and CRAH27 implied 3.13 prices only +84bp of tightening by March 2027. Inference: if US activity/labor stay firm, energy pass-through remains a BoC concern, and Canadian Q2 GDP / Ivey PMI keep activity from collapsing, the BoC has to hike faster or further than that 3.13 mark. The trade pays the March 2027 implied rate because a more resilient cycle closes the gap from 2.29 toward a higher path.
context_build.flow_and_positioning_check: Verified fact: positioning status is partial; CFTC is null and CME positioning is an unavailable market-state source. No packet evidence that CTA, dealer, or leveraged flow explains the CORRA 3.13 mark or the CA-US 2Y extreme. Inference: cannot attribute the cheap Canada path to a documented crowded long-CAD or short-CORRA squeeze. Unknown: holder composition of CRAH27. Treat the price as a policy-path statement until positioning data appear. The existing book already owns this short (pos-dd6fdaf39119, 50m, entry 3.13); this is a hold of that expression, not a new flow-chasing entry.

analogs: 2017-18 synchronized G10 hike cycle: Canada followed a tightening Fed even with mixed domestic data once the global impulse was established; forward outcome was higher Canadian policy rates and a narrower CA-US short-rate gap.

2022 energy-pass-through hiking cycle: central banks that had stayed easy on a core/labor excuse were forced to catch up when headline energy and global tightening persisted. No packet-quantified forward-return table is available, so this is a qualitative analog only.
historical_reference.distribution: Verified fact: CA-US 2Y -140bp sits at the 3.8th 1y and 4.3rd 5y percentiles (z 1y -1.84, z 5y -1.51); CA 2Y 3.27 is stretched versus its 1y history (97.8th) but only mid-pack versus 5y (58.5th); CA 2s10s 56bp is a 1y extreme (0.6th) but a mid 5y reading (65.5th). The 1y stretch is a discovery signal that the front end has already sold and the Canada-US gap is unusually wide; it is not by itself a mean-reversion trade.
historical_reference.regime_differences: Unlike 2022, Canadian core is already near 2% and unemployment is 6.4% with a -42k employment print, so this is not a domestic-overheating analog. Unlike a classic mid-cycle catch-up, the Saudi-Oman workaround has reduced the extreme oil-supply tail even as energy-market shock absorbers are described as weaker. The analog is 'policy too easy versus a global tightening impulse,' not 'Canada is overheating.' NZ sovereign rates are unavailable, so the commodity-bloc comparison is incomplete.

independent_checks: Policy-path check: frozen CORRA strip (overnight 2.29, CRAH27 3.13, terminal near 3.65) versus SOFR (overnight 3.85, SR3H7 4.58, peak 4.755) and the delivered Fed hike to 3.75-4.00%.

Hard-data triangulation: CA activity 66 with Q2 GDP +0.8% q/q and stronger Ivey PMI versus CA labor 38; US activity 69 / labor 75 / inflation 72 with ISM services 55.4 and payrolls +162k; August CA headline CPI 3.0% with core near 2%; NZ Q2 GDP +0.2% q/q beat as a growth-resilience cross-check.
Cross-market rates RV as a check not the trade: CA-US 2Y -140bp at a 1y/5y extreme confirms Canada is the cheap policy pole after the US front end has already sold to the 99.8th 1y percentile.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known: Canada labor is soft (unemployment 6.4%, August employment -42k, wages +2.0% y/y from +2.8%) and core CPI-trim/median are 1.9%/2.0% near target. That labor/core softness is the already-priced excuse for keeping overnight at 2.29 and limiting the hike path. New or newly transmitted: the Fed hike is now delivered, not just >90% priced; the last-24h desk thesis says the energy shock is constraining the global easing impulse and keeping term-rate pressure elevated even where domestic growth is softer; BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through; CA Q2 real GDP printed +0.8% q/q versus revised +0.1% in Q1 and Ivey PMI accelerated; US ISM services 55.4 with activity/new orders above 60 and payrolls +162k with positive revisions. Known labor weakness needs that new global-tightening / activity-rebound transmission to justify a new move in CORRA_2027-03 from 3.13.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: Disagree that 3.13 is enough insurance on March 2027 CORRA. The market is over-weighting the known labor/core softness and under-weighting resilient activity plus a global tightening/energy regime that the desk thesis says is blocking easing. If growth adaptation holds, BoC catch-up should lift the CRAH27 mark, not fade it.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: CRAH27 at 3.13 assumes the BoC delivers a gradual, limited catch-up: only about 84bp by March 2027 and a terminal near 3.65, remaining more than 100bp below the US SR3 peak of 4.755. That path requires Canadian labor softness and near-target core inflation to dominate energy pass-through, the US/Japan tightening impulse, and the Q2 activity rebound. CA-US 2Y at -140bp prices Canada as a structurally easier cycle.

CA 2s10s is 56bp, 0.6th 1y percentile, flattened 18bp in a month as the front end sold. CA-US 2Y is -140bp, 3.8th 1y / 4.3rd 5y. Parallel US path: Fed delivered 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, official SOFR 3.85, SR3H7 4.58 (+73bp). USDCAD rose 1.74% over 1m to 1.401. Inference: the last month was a catch-up selloff in Canadian front-end yields after the Fed hike and energy news, but the futures path still treats Canada as a shallow follower rather than a full participant in the global tightening impulse.

context_build.price_decomposition: Level versus change: overnight 2.29 is the easy starting point; the 3.13 March 2027 implied rate is the priced hike stock; the 1m/3m strip shows almost no near-term move (Oct +1.5bp) and the bulk of tightening stuffed into 2027H1. CA 2s10s flattening to the 0.6th 1y percentile is the front-end selloff, not a growth-collapse steepener. The marginal driver is policy-path catch-up to a tighter global impulse, not a collapse in Canadian term premium. Cross-market: US 2Y 4.76 (99.8th 1y) and SR3 already price a hotter US cycle, so residual edge is in Canada, not in paying already-extreme SOFR.

The CA-US 2Y gap of -140bp is the statistical fingerprint of that underpricing; the executable owner is CRAH27, already marked at 3.13.

Existing short pos-dd6fdaf39119 is still at the packet mid of 3.13; the discrepancy has not closed, so the seat keeps paying the underpriced path rather than rotating into stretched AUDUSD or a USD-contaminated USDCAD short.
